stem: A freezer is at −18°C. During a brownout, its temperature rises by 7°C. What is the temperature now?
hints: Rising means going up, so you add 7. Picture a thermometer: going up from −18 brings you closer to 0.
Write it as −18 + 7. The signs are different, so subtract the sizes: 18 − 7.
18 − 7 gives the size of the answer. Then give it the sign of the number with the bigger size, −18.

solution.methodName: Sign rules for adding and subtracting

steps.action: Write the change as an addition: −18 + 7.
steps.why: The temperature rises, so we add. A temperature below zero is negative.

steps.action: The signs are different (one −, one +), so subtract the sizes: 18 − 7 = 11.
steps.why: When the signs are different, the two numbers partly cancel each other out.

steps.action: Keep the sign of the number with the bigger size. 18 is bigger than 7, and it is negative, so the answer is negative.

trapNotes.−25°C: This is −18 − 7. The temperature rises, so add 7. Going up from −18 brings you closer to 0, not farther from it.
trapNotes.11°C: The size, 11, is right but the sign is wrong. Starting at −18 and going up only 7 degrees, you are still below 0.
trapNotes.25°C: This adds 18 + 7 and ignores the minus sign. The freezer starts below zero, so rising 7 degrees cannot reach 25°C.
